tagline: Stumble through Essos with this Dothraki phrasebook. Impress your friends by butchering 'Qapla'' at the next dinner party.

title: Muppet Master Plan
tagline: Stuck in a meeting that's going nowhere? Distract yourself with this Jim Henson career book, because who wouldn't want to read about puppeteering on company time?

title: Gothic Bridezilla Dreams
tagline: For the bride who wants her wedding to double as a goth club night. Perfect for a midnight ceremony under a full moon, where the only thing brighter than your smile is the glow of your groom’s confused face. Bonus: doubles as a Halloween costume for the rest of your marriage.

title: Hypnotic Puck of Slumber
tagline: Can't stop thinking about that awkward Zoom meeting from 2017? This pulsating metronome-light claims to lull you to sleep. Perfect for insomniacs who also miss the mesmerizing glow of dial-up internet. Just don't blame us when you start dreaming in binary code.

title: The Land Your Desk Demands
tagline: Tired of your miniature figurines staging revolts due to lack of real estate? This patch of simulated terrain is the answer. Finally, a place for tiny plastic knights to contemplate the futility of battle. Just add motivational posters (sold separately). Don't say we never gave you anything.

title: Booze Bandolier: Hydration Hero
tagline: For when your LARPing character is less concerned with slaying dragons and more concerned with maintaining a respectable buzz. This beer-holding holster ensures you're always prepared for extended quests... to the fridge. Holds six cans, because clearly, one in each hand simply isn't efficient enough.

title: Chill Pill Alert
tagline: For when you need to calm down after your cat's Instagram gets more likes than yours, these CBD tablets will help. Because, priorities.

title: Comb Over This, Future
tagline: Dropping six bills to potentially avoid looking like Krusty the Clown in your 50s? Seems reasonable. Especially if your family reunion photos are starting to resemble a before-and-after ad for Rogaine. I mean, who needs a vacation when you can just laser-focus on follicular salvation?

title: Prison Gains, No Chains
tagline: Forget fancy gyms and overpriced trainers. This book is for those who want to get jacked in the most *authentic* way possible—using only your body and a healthy dose of desperation. Perfect for the urban explorer who wants to work out in an abandoned prison or the minimalist who refuses to own dumbbells. Just don’t blame us if you start doing push-ups in the break room.

title: Toe Nail Savior
tagline: For when you've been too lazy to trim your toenails and now they're trying to escape your skin, this tool gently persuades them to grow in a less hostile direction.

title: Air Jordan's Dirty Laundry
tagline: For the friend who still wears Jordan sneakers, this biography is a great way to distract them from their mid-30s basketball delusions. Read about MJ's actual skills, not just their fading memories of him.

title: Snooze on a Plane
tagline: For when you nod off on a redeye and face-plant into the stranger next to you, this J-shaped headrest travel pillow is a weirdly decent solution.

title: Ditch the Dreaded Damp Cast
tagline: So, you thought that interpretive dance performance in the rain was a good idea? Now you're rocking a cast. Don't let a little H2O ruin your post-injury hot tub recovery. This waterproof cover ensures your plaster stays pristine while you soak away the shame.

title: Manly Moisturizer Mayhem
tagline: For the guy who spends more time debating beard oils than actual conversations. Perfect for the bachelor pad where the biggest concern is whether your face cream clashes with your gym bag. Includes a 'manly' scent that smells like a lumberjack’s cologne if he bathed in pine-scented air freshener.

title: Goodfellas: The Book? Fuggedaboutit!
tagline: So, you've already memorized every line of Scorsese's masterpiece, huh? But what about the *footnotes*? For the cinephile who color-codes their Blu-ray collection and dreams of owning a legit garbage truck business, comes the *actual* story. Now you can bore your relatives at Sunday dinner with *even more* obscure trivia.

title: Existential Dread in a Box!
tagline: TheraBox understands: some weeks, a scented candle just won't cut it. When you're staring into the abyss of another unending Zoom meeting, perhaps a curated selection of bath bombs and aromatherapy oils is *exactly* the right level of distraction. At least you'll smell good while questioning everything.

title: Beach Thief Deterrent 3000
tagline: Worried about your valuables while perfecting your sandcastle empire? The AquaVault clamps onto your beach chair, offering questionable security against seasoned towel-snatchers. Perfect for those moments when leaving your phone with Brenda from accounting feels like too much trust.

title: Bourdain’s Brain Dump
tagline: For the armchair traveler who’s already watched every episode of *Parts Unknown* and still wants more. This book is like having Bourdain’s voice in your head during a 3 AM binge on street food documentaries. Perfect for the person who insists their ‘home-cooked’ meal is actually a recreation of a dish they tried in Hanoi once.

title: Piano for People Who Hate People
tagline: Tired of your neighbor’s karaoke sessions? Now you can return the favor with the subtlety of a jackhammer. Perfect for those who want to annoy their roommates, impress their cat, or finally understand why your ex left you. Includes lessons on how to play 'Chopsticks' like a prodigy.

title: Jet-Setter’s Leather Identity Crisis
tagline: For the globetrotter who’s tired of their passport looking like it’s been through a washing machine. This wallet is for the person who needs to prove they’re not a spy at border control—just a very organized one. Perfect for when you’re trying to impress customs with your ‘I travel so much I need a dedicated passport holder’ energy.

title: Pretentious Nomad's Diary
tagline: For the person who wants to document their 'authentic' backpacking experience in a way that screams 'I’m not like other travelers.' Perfect for scribbling down deep thoughts while sipping overpriced coffee in a hostel, or jotting down the names of all the street food you ate before regretting it later. Leather-bound, because nothing says 'adventure' like a fancy journal that costs more than a night in a questionable motel.

title: Soap for People Who Hate Showering
tagline: For the eco-conscious hypochondriac who suspects their last bar of soap was secretly made in a factory by robots. Handcrafted with organic ingredients, because nothing says 'I care about the planet' like paying $20 for something you could make in your kitchen. Perfect for the person who insists their soap must have a backstory, like it was carved by a monk in the Himalayas.

title: Fancy Scribbles for Overthinkers
tagline: For those who’ve ever stared at a blank card for 20 minutes, only to settle on 'Hope you’re doing well.' This kit turns your existential dread into elegant loops and swirls. Perfect for the person who insists their grocery list should look like a royal decree.

title: Swiss Army Existential Dread
tagline: Lost in the woods... again? This isn't just a knife; it's a tiny toolbox of 'maybe I can fix this myself' energy. Perfect for dismantling that Ikea furniture you swore you'd assemble before the next ice age. Or, you know, whittling a tiny boat for your anxieties.

title: Beard Butter for Hipster Vikings
tagline: Because nothing says 'I'm a modern-day lumberjack' like a beard that smells like a fancy candle. Perfect for the guy who wants to look like he just chopped wood but actually spends his days sipping craft beer and debating the merits of different beard oils. This is the stuff that turns your face forest into a silky-smooth woodland retreat.

title: Pocketful of 'Maybe' Justice
tagline: For when you suspect the office potluck chili might be... retaliatory. This keychain multi-tool offers a vague sense of security. It probably won't stop a mugging, but it *might* open that stubborn pickle jar. Or, you know, look intimidating dangling from your keys as you power-walk to your car. Just in case.

title: Brain Food: Questionable Flavor
tagline: Regurgitating facts from the internet gets old. Expand your mind with this hefty tome of trivia. Perfect for those moments when you need to sound marginally more intelligent while cornered at a family gathering. Or, you know, winning that bar trivia night against Chad from accounting.

title: Birthday Candles: Because Fire
tagline: Let's be honest, store-bought cakes are tragically impersonal. These candles? They're a defiant 'I remembered' against the grocery chain abyss. Perfect for when you need to distract from the questionable frosting choices at 3 AM. Also, fire. What's not to love?

title: Embrace Your Inner Idiot
tagline: Ever feel like everyone else is operating on a different plane of logic? This book might explain why. Perfect for the aspiring middle manager trying to decipher their team's baffling decisions, or anyone who's questioned humanity after a trip to the DMV. At least now you'll have a framework for the chaos.

title: Hang Ten...With History?
tagline: Planning a beach vacation with your intensely intellectual, yet terminally uncoordinated, cousin Bartholomew? This deep dive into surfing history might be the only way to get him near the waves without risking a dramatic Coast Guard rescue. At least he'll have something to read *while* he's being rescued.

title: Gonzo Wisdom: Cheap Edition
tagline: So, you're housesitting for a professor who exclusively collects vintage typewriters and taxidermied squirrels. You've accidentally agreed to host his extremely judgmental book club. This biography of Hunter S. Thompson is probably the only thing preventing you from serving boxed wine and faking a sudden illness. At least it's cheaper than therapy.

title: Die Trying, Maybe
tagline: For the friend who's stuck in a rut, give them 101 things to do before they actually die from boredom. Like, what's next, a bucket list for leaving the house?

title: Cosmos in a Flash
tagline: Stuck in an elevator with a physics nerd? This book saves you from awkward small talk about black holes.

title: Nautical Existential Crisis
tagline: For the friend who's questioning life's meaning on a solo sailing trip, this book is a $50 anchor to their existential dread.

title: Joy in a Brick
tagline: Stuck in a never-ending DMV line? This 14,000-item happiness catalog is your sanity saver. Because who needs human interaction when you can read about delightful things?

title: Float Like Book
tagline: For when you're stuck in a waiting room with a boxing enthusiast, this Muhammad Ali book is a decent conversation starter, or a last resort to avoid discussing the weather.
